common_name: Bausei Dumb Cane (Historic Veitch Hybrid Dieffenbachia)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix; move outdoors only after nights stay above 60°F and bring back in before fall cold.

directions: Bausei is one of the older named dumb cane hybrids, raised at the Veitch nursery in the 1870s and named for the Chelsea foreman who selected it, predating most of today's mass-market dieffenbachia cultivars. Its paddle-shaped leaves are pale yellow-green overlaid with irregular dark green blotching and fine cream-white speckling that runs out along a whitish midrib, giving it a softer, more muted look than high-contrast modern selections like Camille or Honeydew. Like other dieffenbachias it grows as an upright, cane-like stem that sheds its lowest leaves as it matures, so plan to stake or cut back leggy canes to keep it full. Keep soil evenly moist but never soggy, provide bright indirect light and high humidity, and handle with care since the sap causes painful oral and skin irritation if chewed or rubbed into eyes.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Dieffenbachia Species for Florida Interiors

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in rich, well-drained potting mix, keeping it indoors year-round outside zones 10-11.

directions: Memoria Corsii stands apart from most dumb canes for its cool, silvery-gray leaf ground color, deepened by dark green veining and a narrow dark green margin rather than the cream, white, or gold patterning typical of the genus. The broad, oval leaves are held on a shorter, more compact cane than vigorous cultivars like Tropic Marianne, making it a good fit for tabletop or low-light interior display. Provide bright, indirect light, evenly moist soil, and humidity above 50 percent to keep the leaf color from dulling, and repot every couple of years as the rhizomatous base fills its container. As with all dieffenbachias, the sap is loaded with calcium oxalate crystals and causes intense mouth and throat irritation if ingested, so keep it away from pets and small children.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Dieffenbachia Species for Florida Interiors
